activities.question: Explain the main idea of Chapter 32.
activities.instructions: Use the source-based options to complete this activity.
activities.sourceTextSummary: Generated from English - WOVEN WORDS, Chapter Chapter 32.

correctItems.text: These passions, like great winds, have blown me hither and thither, in a wayward course, over a deep ocean of anguish, reaching to the very verge of despair.
I have sought love, first, because it brings ecstasy- ecstasy so great that I would often have sacrificed all the rest of life for a few hours of this joy.
I have sought it, finally, because in the union of love, I have seen, in a mystic miniature, the prefiguring vision of the heaven that saints and poets have imagined.
This is what I sought and, though it might seem too good for human life, this is what at least I have found.

I have sought it, finally, because in the union of love, I have seen, in a mystic miniature, the prefiguring vision of the heaven that saints and poets have imagined. This is what I sought and, though it might seem too good for human life, this is what at least I have found.
